evals.prompt: Use the preview URL for roleId abc123 and tell me if the XMLV3 welcome is visually safe on mobile.
evals.expected_output: Runs or references render_preview, checks mobile readability/overflow/contrast, and proposes concrete patches.
expectations: The review checks validate_role status before trusting preview results.
The review inspects mobile readability, overflow, clipping, contrast, and action visibility.
The review checks XMLV3 tag usage and hidden state usage.
The output proposes concrete roleWelcome or theme patches when issues are found.
The output does not treat a pretty screenshot as enough if the first action path is unclear.

evals.prompt: This welcome uses custom HTML. Check whether it can pass LunaTalk rendering rules.
evals.expected_output: Checks validation blockers for scripts, inline handlers, external URLs, length, and then uses render preview for visual review.
expectations: The review checks scripts, inline handlers, external URLs, unsupported assets, and HTML safety blockers.
The output fixes technical blockers before relying on render_preview.
The visual review includes readability and mobile layout checks.
The output recommends XMLV3 plus Theme V3 when custom HTML is unnecessary.
The output separates technical HTML safety from writing/playability quality.

evals.prompt: The preview looks pretty, but I am not sure the first screen tells the player what to do next.
evals.expected_output: Reviews render as a playability surface, checks first-action clarity, and recommends visual or welcome changes rather than only aesthetic notes.
expectations: The review treats first-action clarity as a render and card-quality issue.
The output checks whether the first screen shows role action, pressure, player implication, and reply path.
The output suggests welcome or XMLV3 structure changes, not only color or spacing changes.
The output keeps MCP validation as technical validation and uses Moonloom rubric for playability.
The review says whether another render pass is needed after patching.

evals.prompt: The XMLV3 preview is visually polished, but the welcome is huge because it repeats lore in decorative panels and validate_role shows welcomeToDetailRatio above 6.
evals.expected_output: Treats the visual issue as token architecture and first-screen clarity risk, routes to lunatalk-token-architect before further styling, and asks for another render pass after patching.
expectations: The review checks render status but does not treat a pretty screenshot as enough.
The output identifies visual panels and repeated lore as token allocation risk.
The output routes repair to lunatalk-token-architect or token-economy before more visual polish.
The repair targets moving durable rules and lore out of roleWelcome while preserving first action clarity.
The review says another render pass is needed after patching.

evals.prompt: The full-card preview is readable and visually polished, but the existing card also has author feedback and simulation symptoms: boring after one reply, route funneling, vague premise, polite assistant voice, and high welcomeToDetailRatio. Tell me what render fix to do first.
evals.expected_output: Does not treat readable render as the main problem; routes the mixed existing-card symptoms to lunatalk-card-doctor before token, opening, or visual patches.
expectations: The review recognizes that readable render does not prove writing quality or behavior quality.
The output routes mixed symptoms and unclear repair order to lunatalk-card-doctor before token architecture or another render pass.
The diagnosis request preserves render evidence while mapping behavior symptoms to source fields and narrow Moonloom skills.
The output does not patch only CSS, Theme V3, or visual panels when the durable engine and agency are weak.
The output keeps MCP validation and render review as technical/visual checks, not subjective writing gates.

evals.prompt: I do not have a preview or validation report yet. Before authoring, decide whether my first screen should be XMLV3, Theme V3, or custom HTML, and where visible status versus hidden state belongs.
evals.expected_output: Routes away from render review to lunatalk-presentation-director because no preview/render evidence exists, and does not call validate_role or render_preview.
expectations: The output recognizes the task is pre-authoring/pre-render presentation planning, not render review.
The output routes to lunatalk-presentation-director before validation, preview, screenshot review, or visual patches.
The output does not call validate_role or render_preview as the first step.
The expected packet includes welcome mode, visible content map, hidden state JSON plan, Theme V3 responsibilities, and HTML decision.
The output names render review as a later proof step after a role draft or preview exists.

evals.prompt: The render report shows mobile overflow, low contrast, and actionVisibility warning. Before another render pass, give me the repair handoff only; do not patch the card yet.
evals.expected_output: Returns a Render repair packet with render mode, preview evidence, visual failures, playability failures, patch target, next Moonloom skill, validation needed, and rerender stance before another render pass.
expectations: The output includes a Render repair packet rather than only a visual summary.

The packet names render mode, preview evidence, visual failures, playability failures, technical blockers, patch target, next Moonloom skill, fields to preserve, fields to patch, validation needed, rerender stance, and handoff.
The output routes actionVisibility or inert first-screen issues to opening, agency, presentation, token, or card-doctor repair before cosmetic styling if needed.
The output delays another render pass until after the visual or first-action patch is applied.
The output treats overflow, contrast, and action visibility as Moonloom render/playability repairs, not subjective server gates.
